💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that coros has unveiled the Vertix 4, an “expedition-focused” upgrade to the Vertix 2 and 2S.
  • This watch is being marketed as a major step up from the Vertix 2S, with an AMOLED display, a more refined design, satellite maps and, for the first time on a Coros watch, a built-in flashlight.
  • That price does still undercut the latest Garmin Fenix 9 line-up, which starts at $999, though some rivals are cheaper still.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that coros has unveiled the Vertix 4, an “expedition-focused” upgrade to the Vertix 2 and 2S. Coros states it pairs the brand's brightest display yet with long battery life, and after unboxing it myself, I can definitely say it has a more refined feel that could indeed suit the office as well as the summit.

This watch is being marketed as a major step up from the Vertix 2S, with an AMOLED display, a more refined design, satellite maps and, for the first time on a Coros watch, a built-in flashlight. The Vertix 4 will be available to buy starting on Black Friday, Nov. 27, but it won't exactly be at a discount: It costs $799, a $100 increase over the Vertix 2S.

That price does still undercut the latest Garmin Fenix 9 line-up, which starts at $999, though some rivals are cheaper still. For instance, the Suunto Vertical 2 steel model costs $599, and the Garmin Fenix 8 is currently on sale for $749.99 at Amazon.

I've only just started testing the Vertix 4 and haven't even had enough time to get through its substantial battery life, but I can share some first impressions, particularly in how it compares with the Garmin Fenix 9 Pro that rolled out earlier this year.

Built-in flashlights have become a must-have feature on premium sports watches, and now the Vertix 4 is the first Coros watch to get one. Coros has departed from the usual layout, though. Garmin, Suunto and Amazfit put the light on top of the watch, but Coros places it on the side, between the digital dial and the back button.

Previous Vertix watches used a memory-in-pixel (MIP) display. MIP has advantages, most notably longer battery life, but I know I much prefer the vibrant display on AMOLED screens, like on the Vertix 4. It is the biggest visual change and a large part of why the watch looks more premium than its predecessors.

Sources indicate that coros claims up to 30 days in watch mode, or 10 days with the screen always on. It also quotes 48 hours of multi-band GPS tracking with the screen always on. I haven't had time to test these claims properly, so stay tuned.

Coros watches are high-quality sports watches, but don't expect to find all the little lifestyle features you've come to expect on a more traditional smartwatch:.

According to recent reports, music: It can store tracks, but only files you drag and drop onto the watch. It doesn't pair with streaming services.

Payments: There is no NFC payment support.

Watch faces: Customization is more limited than on rivals.

On paper, the Vertix 4 looks like a significant upgrade: a better display, a more attractive design, a flashlight and satellite maps, at a price well below the Fenix 9 line-up. The $100 increase and cheaper alternatives like the Suunto Vertical 2 and discounted Fenix 8 will matter to some buyers, as will the limited smart features.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Steam isn't running an official Black Friday fest—it notes so right here in this enhancement, "Steam isn't running an official Black Friday fest"—but plenty of game developers have marked their stuff down to take advantage of the big sale season, and so Valve is helping them all out a bit by "dressing up" its Discounts and Events page in the appropriate seasonal garb.

In a recent development, is there a little bit of wink wink, nudge nudge to that 'not a Black Friday fest' business? Hey, maybe.

In fair play, though, Steam traditionally hasn't run Black Friday sales, because its Autumn Sale was always happening at the same time. The realignment of seasonal sales in 2025 changed that, however, leaving a hole that was filled by the first-ever Steam Black Friday Sale last year.

Sources indicate that valve has other priorities this year, though, which could explain the absence (wink wink, nudge nudge) of an official Black Friday event on Steam in 2026. In September, Valve confirmed changes to Steam's Discounts and Events page to make it prettier and more personalized, and it said in today's enhancement that Black Friday is "the perfect time to share the updates we've been working on to make the Discounts & Events page a better experience altogether.".

Recent findings suggest that with that all cleared up, I'll say that the Black Friday non-fest page is definitely an eye-catcher, and it will be interesting to see how Valve puts this section of Steam to work in the future. If it's treated like an 'almost a Steam sale' that never really ends, I have to think that developers and gamers alike will benefit—at least until we all get used to it and Valve has to figure out some newly introduced way to tweak the formula.

For now, since we're here, let's check out some deals:.

And here's one other difference between actual Steam sales and the Black Friday non-event: Valve said the Black Friday decor will come off the Discounts and Events page on November 30, but the discounts themselves all have separate end dates. The Divinity: Original Sin 2 sale, for instance, also ends on November 30, but Outer Wilds will stay marked down until December 5, and the Esoteric Ebb deal will be valid until December 7.

Another Gaming Console Price Hike Could Be Coming, Thanks To New Tariffs

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (718 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamespot

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that the US government has announced a new round of tariffs targeting several major countries, including China, Japan, Vietnam, and European Union trading partners.
  • In a recent development, the US government has unveiled a fresh round of tariffs targeting several major countries, including China, Japan, Vietnam, and European Union trading partners.
  • What does this mean for gaming hardware?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the US government has announced a new round of tariffs targeting several major countries, including China, Japan, Vietnam, and European Union trading partners. Under the proposed tariffs, import taxes will rise significantly, with China facing up to 40% when the new duties take effect next year. According to the BBC, some of the rates will be reduced because of tariff caps that US President Donald Trump has already agreed to, and individual countries could also face different levies. What does this mean for gaming hardware? Trump's first round of "Liberation Day" tariffs contributed to rising console prices, but the Supreme Court eventually struck them down. Big companies like Sony, Microsoft, and Nintendo benefited from tariff refunds after the ruling, but they didn't pass the savings on to consumers. In Sony's case, it was estimated to get back $508 million in refunds from the US government. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4FatSqS3VYY&t=19s The new tariffs bypass the Supreme Court's ruling by using a different law, Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, which allows the government to impose tariffs on countries that use unfair business practices. The law does require an investigation into specific trade practices before rates are set. If higher import taxes take effect, console companies could face much higher costs, and protecting their profits will likely mean consumers have to cover the difference. Nintendo, Sony, and Microsoft have moved much of their final assembly out of China and into Southeast Asia, especially Vietnam, to avoid earlier tariffs. However, key parts like batteries and power supplies still mostly come from China, and if tariffs on these parts rise, total production costs for consoles made outside China will go up even more. Some electronic goods could be exempt from tariffs, and manufacturers often stockpile inventory ahead of tariff deadlines to delay price changes. But with rising costs from the ongoing components shortage amid the AI boom and other global factors, console prices remain at risk. After the June announcement of steep console price hikes, Microsoft warned that Xbox console costs could rise again in 2027, and next-gen hardware is also expected to be very pricey.

GTA 6 Is A Tragedy Because You Cannot Sit Down And Eat Spaghetti

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1441 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Kotaku

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that everyone, including me, has been making much (rightfully) of how incredible the level of detail in GTA VI is.
  • It has been revealed that you cannot sit down and enjoy a slow, relaxing meal.
  • I love cooking through video game cookbooks, I love beautifully designed and rendered meals within game worlds, and I love creative food crafting systems.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6Grand Theft Auto VI.

Recent findings suggest that everyone, including me, has been making much (rightfully) of how incredible the level of detail in GTA VI is. This game is ridiculous, man! The sheer amount of incidental and specific dialogue, the clothing, the way characters move, the weather, the TV and radio programs, I could go on all day. But there’s a single aspect I’ve found where the level of detail genuinely felt short of what I’d hoped for going in: the food.

It has been revealed that you cannot sit down and enjoy a slow, relaxing meal. There is nowhere to order a plate of spaghetti or other food to be eaten explicitly there, in the establishment. There is no cooking. There is only fast food and takeout. And that’s how I know this game is going to be a tragedy.

I love video game food. I love cooking through video game cookbooks, I love beautifully designed and rendered meals within game worlds, and I love creative food crafting systems. So I’m always on the lookout for such things! And in one respect, I actually think GTA VIÂ does food beautifully. It isÂ freaking incredible that you can hold a food and a drink (or two foods, or two drinks) in each hand simultaneously, and swap between consuming each of them at will. Last night, I took Lucia out to a food truck and bought an empanada and a mojito. I had her stand there and take bites of the empanada, and watched with wonder as the empanada disappeared, bite by bite in her hand. (I tried to take a sip of the mojito but accidentally pulled my gun instead and someone called the cops, but I’m sure it would have been equally impressive).

According to recent reports, much has been made of this system, and deservedly. Jason takes bites of apples, and the apples having those bites visible in them until only the core is left! The pair will drink liquids, and you can see the liquids in the containers slowly recede! All of these items have unique models, too: burgers, tacos, croissants, the grilled fish sandwiches made in an early mission that have different levels of char as Jason cooks them…God, it’s incredible! Hats off!

I don’t want anything about that system to change. I love being able to eat handheld foods like this. But what bothers me is that this is…all that Jason and Lucia ever eat.

I complained about this earlier, after a glimpse in the pair’s fridge in an early trailer. Mostly alcohol and protein shakes. Nothing substantial whatsoever to keep two active crime-doers properly fed. But at the time, I thought that was just…their state at that moment in the game. I assumed eventually the pair would end up in a situation where they ate food like normal human beings.

It has been revealed that yet this never happens. I’m in chapter 3, and I’ve consulted with our reviewer who has finished the game, and my understanding is that the pair will never evolve beyond eating on the go. You can’t order a plate of spaghetti or some lo mein and sit comfortably and lazily consume it. The pair never cooks food at home, either as a mechanic or even as a visual suggestion, as their cabinets remain full of nothing but plain bread and cereal and unused pots and pans right up until the end of the game. Every restaurant that looks like it could be a proper sit-down dining establishment is closed and locked to you, and everything that’s open serves like, five things: water, soda, beer, and roughly two handheld food items. And those same 10-20 food items are repeated ad nauesum across all the game’s restaurants, regardless of what’s on the posted menu. In a small handful of establishments, you can sit down to eat those items, but it still doesn’t look like the two are relaxing over a meal. Again, I understood this early in the gameâthe two were broke, Jason was living a bachelor life, and they were on the run. Hell, the motel room in Chapter 2 doesn’t even have its own coffee pot. I get it.

In a recent development, but as the two move to Vice City, build wealth, and start living at a higher standard, I really just thought there’d be some option, somewhere, for one of them to take the other out on a nice dinner date. Maybe just a little cutscene showing a decent plate of food with the two all dolled up. Or perhaps, if that was too risky, the barest suggestion that either of them had ever cooked at home: TV trays, or a dirty pot in the sink, or more than like four spices sitting in the window for some reason. Even like, aÂ discussion about having eaten a meal?

Sources indicate that so on one level, I’m disappointed. I love seeing gorgeous food renders in games, and I can only imagine Rockstar’s would be stellar. I think a lot about how the Dragon’s Dogma team bought expensive steak just so they could film themselves cooking it for the game. Or the absurd feasting scenes in Monster Hunter with gorgeous cheese naan. Or even the very simple scenes in the Yakuza games, where you couldn’t see the food, but you could hear the characters discussing how it tasted and what their thoughts were. Impressive as the handheld food is, I’m not really excited at making Jason eat another croissant after I’ve seen the animation a few times. He doesn’t talk about it, it doesn’t seem to do anything for him, he doesn’t even really seem to derive any pleasure from it. Just a health boost maybe.

According to recent reports, but even as I’m disappointed by all the storefronts I can’t enter and the menus I read but can never get Jason or Lucia to order from and eat, I’m starting to get what GTA VI is trying to say here. It’s not a budget or a time glitch, I know that. If Rockstar devs had wanted to make gorgeous food or record discussions about eating it, they would have. I really do think GTA VI wants to convey in every possible way that this pair will never, ever be safe. They will not be able to slow down or stop or rest for the kind of luxurious meal I want them to have. And that’s luxury not even just in terms of spending lots of money on nice food, but the luxury of time and safety: spending the time to sit, in public, and eat it regardless of where that is. The kind of luxury I feel when my husband and I go to our favorite local Indian joint and, instead of ordering takeout, sit and eat out of the metal trays and sip chai and share naan. If Jason and Lucia sit to eat at all, it will always be in chairs that are easily pushed out, in empty greasy spoons where they can make a quick getaway.

In a recent development, I suspect that wherever the story is going, it is not going to a place where they will be able to comfortably enjoy a slow glass of wine and a fine risotto. It’s not even that it’s an option I can see on the horizon, out of reach due to price or other limitations. It is just, permanently and forever, not for them. Maybe I’ll be proven wrong, and there will be a perfect, peaceful, happy ending where the pair get to live a normal life with their son in a safe place with minimal crime, and where they can go out for a significant plate of spaghetti that all three can sit down to enjoy over a wonderful hour of laughter and merriment. Maybe there’s a world where someone could reasonably imagine the three enjoying a multi-hour, homecooked Thanksgiving together. But given all the crime I’ve been doing, somehow I feel that a happy and normal future will, like the many, many restaurants of Leonida, be forever closed to them.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that here it was, the major reveal.
  • In a recent development, about 42 seconds after it started, things went off the rails.
  • Industry observers note that the setting was the Cotillion Ballroom, the chandeliered 4,000-square-foot event space at New York’s iconic Pierre Hotel, the site of Al Pacino’s blind tango in Scent of a Woman, where the ceilings are 19 feet high, the curtains are golden, and the windows offer views of Central Park’s southeast corner.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that here it was, the major reveal. After years of planning and wrangling, after more than $10 million spent on engineers and lawyers and architects, after all of the rumors and headlines and finger-pointing, the long-awaited presentation was ready to be made.

In a recent development, about 42 seconds after it started, things went off the rails. A “shitshow,” as multiple people would later describe to Vanity Fair the two-and-a-half-hour meeting on the morning of July 29.

Industry observers note that the setting was the Cotillion Ballroom, the chandeliered 4,000-square-foot event space at New York’s iconic Pierre Hotel, the site of Al Pacino’s blind tango in Scent of a Woman, where the ceilings are 19 feet high, the curtains are golden, and the windows offer views of Central Park’s southeast corner. Seated at round tables were 40 or so of the people with enough disposable income to call the Pierre home, or at least a home: investor Austin Hearst; Tory Burch, the fashion powerhouse; Lois Chiles, the 1970s-era movie star and model. Joining remotely was Michael Eisner, the former Disney CEO, who last year spent $4.3 million to buy a second apartment there and, with it, even more shares in the co-op that owns the Pierre.

According to recent reports, in came representatives from the Khashoggi Holding Organization out of Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, and the Dorchester Collection, the luxury hotel management firm owned by the Sultan of Brunei. Their proposition was straightforward. Khashoggi wanted to buy the Pierre—the nearly 200-room hotel and all of the apartments too—for $2 billion, less expenses. It was an enormous haul, even for a neighborhood this tony. And it would be all in cash. “The funds are right now available,” a Khashoggi representative promised.

It has been revealed that but if the residents with two thirds of the co-op’s shares accepted the offer, everyone would have to move out. Neighbors would be voting, in effect, to force their fellow neighbors from their apartments.

It would be in their best interest, the Dorchester and Khashoggi reps remarked. The Pierre was a gem, but a tarnished one after 96 summers and thousands of guests. It didn’t have many of the amenities that come standard these days in a five-star hotel. The façade was already undergoing a $22 million overhaul, and there were deeper, systemic problems to solve. The CEO of the company managing the Pierre publicly complained it was something of a money pit. All of that would change after Khashoggi bought the place, the presenters promised. Dorchester would invest more than $1 billion into the Pierre, giving the landmark building a grand new entrance on 61st Street, a pool in the basement, and structural renovations throughout.

When it was done, the residents would be first in line to buy apartments at the all-new, all-modern Dorchester-managed Pierre, ready to last another century.

Sources indicate that the response in the Cotillion room was instant and not particularly friendly. Some residents had moved in not long ago. Others had spent millions remodeling their apartments. “How are we going to enjoy all the perks of this wonderfully renewed building when we’re forced to sell at a price you determine and we have to buy reconfigured apartments, not our own, at market prices?” asked Tina Beriro, the philanthropist and longtime resident, in a recording of the meeting reviewed by Vanity Fair. Like many of the residents, Beriro, at 85, was only a few years younger than the hotel itself. “Many of us are going to be dead by the time you finish.”.

Sources indicate that christopher Cowdray, Dorchester’s white-haired, Zimbabwe-born president, didn’t have an answer. Nor did he provide much of a response when asked what would happen to the more than 400 people who work at the hotel. “In this case, we are still in discussion at the moment,” Cowdray said, to audible groans.

“Many employees have worked here 30 and 40 years and are just about to hit retirement,” Burch pointed out, per the recording. “I have people in the elevator crying that they feel like their job is on the line.”.

According to recent reports, the questions kept coming. For years, shareholders had begged—and even sued—to find out more about the sale. But the long-promised detailed intends for the Pierre’s purchase were still weeks away, adding to the tension in the Cotillion room. (One source, very much in favor of a sale, later called the decision to make an elaborate presentation to the shareholders without those specifics “idiotic.”).

According to recent reports, “Look, ladies and gentlemen, I’ve been on the board of the Hearst Corporation for over 25 years. Sat on the boards of many corporations, for profit and not for profit. I have never seen anything like this,” Hearst noted, his voice cracking. “This is a serious problem that you have presented to the shareholders, and you guys have done a miserable fucking job.”.

One of the many lawyers in the room interrupted him, and they started going at it. Cowdray and the other presenters were escorted out. At one point, the wife of Michael Stern, the 88-year-old chairman of the co-op’s board, tried to offer his resignation on his behalf (which he then turned down). Even by the famously hostile standards of Upcoming York City’s high-end co-ops, this was nasty.

Ironically, the co-op’s biggest shareholder—the resident with the most at stake in the sale financially—didn’t show up. Howard Lutnick was busy in the Oval Office that day with President Donald Trump in his role as US commerce secretary.

Lutnick had bought the Pierre’s 16-room penthouse, its largest apartment, in 2017 for $44 million. If the sale of the Pierre were to go through, Lutnick would get as much as $100 million for the penthouse, even as his neighbors were forced to sell and hundreds of hotel staffers’ jobs were put in jeopardy. Newmark Group—the real estate services firm hired by the Pierre’s board and controlled by Cantor Fitzgerald, the brokerage house previously run by Lutnick—would earn tens of millions more.

It has been revealed that newmark may have a reputation for shepherding massive-ticket sales to completion. But in a letter to the Pierre’s board last year, Beriro called the hiring of the Lutnick-linked firm “a blatant conflict of interest,” an allegation sources close to Lutnick and the board deny. One Pierre resident tells me that Lutnick’s involvement is symbolic of a “culture of corruption” that extends from 1600 Pennsylvania Avenue in Washington to the edges of Central Park in New York. Others imply it is part of a different pattern: the purchase of more and more of America’s most valuable assets by companies and sovereign wealth funds from the Persian Gulf’s petrostates, at times orchestrated by those in and around the second Trump administration. Those shareholders wonder whether Lutnick had personally worked behind the scenes to maneuver the Khashoggi group into place to buy the Pierre, and that speculation spilled onto the pages of The New York Times.

BALL GAMES Guests attend a Valentino party in the Cotillion Ballroom at the Pierre hotel, 1970, New York.

In a recent development, A source close to Lutnick notes that he formally cut ties with Newmark in early 2025 and adds that, since his move to government, Lutnick’s only involvement in the Pierre sales process has been to respond to media reports like this one. A spokesperson for Sabre Park Avenue LLC, Khashoggi’s American holding firm, tells Vanity Fair in a statement that “any insinuation or implication that the proposal, the transaction or the parties involved engaged in improper or undisclosed conduct is categorically false.”.

I spoke to more than 15 sources and reviewed hundreds of pages of documents related to the Pierre deal, including previously unreported text messages between Lutnick and Khashoggi and a corporate intelligence dossier dropped in my mailbox.

Turns out, the shareholders were right to wonder about Lutnick’s role.

The Pierre for decades was synonymous with Upcoming York glamour. At the height of their star power, Audrey Hepburn stayed in the hotel’s suites and Elizabeth Taylor kept an apartment there. The restaurant’s original menu was created by Escoffier. Barbara Walters had a reception for her final wedding at the Pierre (about 10 years after she and my grandfather, the Broadway producer Lee Guber, officially split). Yves Saint Laurent owned a two-bedroom on the 38th floor, which was later bought by Valentino cofounder Giancarlo Giammetti, who then sold it to former Bottega Veneta creative director Tomas Maier.

And yet for 15 years or more, there’s been a growing sense that the Pierre’s best days are behind it, even as the stars continue to use the hotel to get ready for the Met Gala. A 2010 Wall Street Journal article mentions how the Pierre “lost its glory.” By the time Lutnick swooped in to buy the penthouse in 2017, he did so at an $81 million discount off its original asking price.

THE TORY PARTY Fashion designer Tory Burch, in one of the hotel’s elevators, was among the residents opposed to the sale.

Since then, age has continued to take its toll. Scaffolding has surrounded the hotel since at least 2018, according to city records. Exit a multimillion-dollar apartment with a spectacular view of the park and you’re liable to find worn carpets or hallways with the faint odor of mold. Rooms at the Pierre tend to cost much less than they do at the Plaza or the Ritz-Carlton, just around the corner.

Industry observers note that over time, a group of shareholders became particularly vexed with Taj Hotels, which had managed the property since 2005. There were complaints of broken elevators, empty concierge desks, and “slipshod maintenance.” Maier, in an October 2023 co-op-wide email, lamented that Taj delayed long-planned renovations to his apartment for months, citing high hotel occupancy. (A Taj spokesperson remarked in a statement those concerns “reflected a specific point in time rather than the overall trajectory of the property.”).

What Maier may not have known—and what the residents I spoke to were unaware of—was that the Pierre’s board had already explored the possibility of replacing Taj. The only way to do that, to break the contract with Taj, was to sell the Pierre. In April 2023, the board drafted a memorandum of understanding with the Maybourne Hotel Group, which is primarily owned by members of the Qatari royal family, to buy the hotel portion of the Pierre. “But there was a condition,” a source familiar with the matter tells me. “Everybody had to move out for two years.” The source adds, “You cannot renovate a 100-year-old building with people living in it, right?”.

In a recent development, that was a deal killer. So the board decided, in this source’s words, to hire a firm that could broker a “more acceptable” sale. They picked the real estate consultancy Newmark. Lutnick was still chairman of Newmark’s board at that time, though two sources say he had no role in the decision. (The board, through its attorney, declined to comment for this story. But a Newmark spokesperson says its “unanimous” selection was “based on the firm’s experience advising on some of Newly introduced York City’s most complex and high-profile real estate transactions.”).

From there, “Newmark went out to find another buyer,” the first source adds. Its fee at the time: $50,000 per month, to be counted against any future commissions in the event of a sale. (Eventually that was bargained down to a flat $30 million.) The board retained the high-profile law firm Fried Frank, which had represented Lutnick’s companies before, to assist Newmark in its search.

LONDON'S CALLING Christopher Cowdray, the Dorchester Collection’s president, was part of the contentious presentation to residents in the Cotillion ballroom at the Pierre.

Since Lutnick’s financial firm, Cantor Fitzgerald, owned a controlling stake in Newmark, that gave Lutnick an incentive to see the Pierre sold. He had another: According to the source connected to Lutnick, his 12,000-square-foot penthouse triplex had been uninhabitable since 2021, when a storm had caused catastrophic damage. Lutnick concluded, according to the source close to him, that major repairs wouldn’t make sense if they weren’t accompanied by a larger round of structural renovations to the building. In the meantime, he installed a basketball court in the apartment to make some use of the place.

When the sales process started, the idea was to make a deal for the hotel only. The new owner would likely want to consolidate guest rooms on certain floors. That meant some Pierre residents might be encouraged—strongly encouraged—to sell, but not necessarily everyone.

Brokers approached everyone from Mark Zuckerberg to Michael Dell to the king of Morocco to buy the place. Most of the residents were in the dark. As far as they knew, Newmark was trying to help renovate the building, not sell it off. Nor did they know Lutnick was personally trying to wrangle potential buyers for the Pierre.

On Wednesday, May 8, 2024, Lutnick’s private jet took off from Teterboro, Newly introduced Jersey, outside of New York. Lutnick was on his way to Paris to meet with the Arnault family who, as part of their dominion over LVMH, run the Cheval Blanc hotel group. The source close to Lutnick mentions he had long admired the hotels and pitched the idea of the Pierre joining the group.

It has been revealed that lutnick’s first stop, however, was in London. After his plane landed, he went to the Dorchester Collection’s eponymous hotel in Mayfair. Shortly after 9 a.m. on Thursday, Lutnick gathered with Cowdray, the Dorchester president, and Motasem Khashoggi, chairman and principal owner of the Khashoggi Holding Company. From the outside, it seemed like an unlikely trio. The Khashoggi family was mainly famous for its wealth, but that was decades ago, back when Adnan, Motasem’s relative, was one of the world’s leading arms dealers. Motasem is recognized internationally today not as a captain of Saudi industry but as the primary legal representative for the Khashoggi family following the brutal 2018 murder of his journalist cousin, Jamal, by the Saudi state.

The source close to Lutnick notes he and Khashoggi “met and spoke about a variety of different things” in London, “including: Wouldn’t it be cool if the Pierre was a Dorchester Collection hotel.” Eight days after the London meeting, according to screenshots of WhatsApp messages reviewed by Vanity Fair, Khashoggi texted Lutnick to say that “Brunie”—Hassanal Bolkiah, the Sultan of Brunei, who owns the Dorchester Collection—had “directly” asked him to explore a deal for the Pierre.

Khashoggi then asked Lutnick if he could give one of his kids a summer internship and provided his phone number. (Vanity Fair verified that number, as well as the ones used by Lutnick and the elder Khashoggi in the chats.) Lutnick promptly agreed to the father’s request. “We would be delighted to have your son join us,” he wrote. “I’m excited to invest in and build exciting companies together.”.

A week later, Khashoggi sent the chat his greetings “from rainy Frankfurt,” along with a draft letter of intent to the Pierre’s board to begin due diligence for a “potential acquisition of The Pierre Hotel” and a strategy to buy up “the remaining residential units.”.

Lutnick wrote back on Memorial Day. “I am flying to Europe this evening, Italy and France,” he texted. “I’ve made a few modifications to the letter of intent.” Promise a “complete renovation of the guest rooms, public areas, dining facilities, and amenities,” Lutnick suggested. And be sure to include target prices, both per room and for the whole thing.

Recent findings suggest that lutnick’s firm, Newmark, was supposed to be representing the sellers in this transaction. Yet here Lutnick was coaching potential buyers, in effect putting himself on both sides of the deal. It wasn’t a cardinal sin in the take-no-prisoners worlds of Latest York City real estate or MAGA politics, but it wasn’t strictly kosher either.

Lutnick was confirmed as commerce secretary in February 2025; he stepped down from his Newmark chairmanship then and transferred his Cantor Fitzgerald assets to his sons. Lutnick was still listed as a member of the Pierre’s “transaction committee” in March, when the board confirmed in a letter that Newmark was in negotiations with an unnamed “operator.” But not to worry, the board added: “No owner would be required to sell their unit or move to another one.”.

Sources indicate that residents scrambled to find out more. All they got back were rumors and whispers. One shareholder’s representative indicates he heard the chatter but “blew it off,” thinking that nervous residents were being “dramatic.” According to this representative, the attorneys at Holland & Knight, which had represented the Pierre for years, seemed to be in the dark as well. “You can’t sell a co-op. Never happening here,” one of those lawyers told the representative in this source’s recounting. (Holland & Knight declined to comment for this story.).

In June 2025, the Latest York Post reported that the Sultan of Brunei was in talks to buy the Pierre, along with Essam ­Khashoggi, an older relative of Motasem’s. The board, chaired by Michael Stern, didn’t provide many specifics in a July Zoom with shareholders but emphasized that a sale was in their best interest, according to multiple published accounts. Two months later, according to court filings, four co-op board members—the investor John Levin, former Coca-Cola CEO Douglas Daft, the lawyer and movie producer David G. Johnson, and former KB Home chief executive Bruce Karatz—approved a nonbinding term sheet to sell the Pierre.

Recent findings suggest that on September 16, at a gathering in the Cotillion Ballroom, Fried Frank lawyers broke the news to shareholders. Khashoggi Holding was the buyer, and the sultan’s Dorchester Collection would be the hotel’s managers. The price was astronomical, they stated, and would guarantee residents “at least three times the market value” for their apartments, Town & Country reported. But the transaction was different from the one discussed back in March. It was not just for the hotel and selected apartments. It was for the whole building, which meant the co-op owners had to vacate within 12 months. All of them.

BREAKFAST NEAR TIFFANY'S A young woman enjoys room service at the Pierre Hotel, 1943.

According to recent reports, an escrow account of $10 million, funded by the shareholders, would be “used for eviction proceedings” for any residents who refused to leave, according to a slideshow presentation delivered by the lawyers that day. And on that happy note, residents were encouraged to open the personalized envelopes that had been given to them at the door, one for each shareholder. Inside were estimates of how much they might get from a sale.

It has been revealed that one person who was there indicates it reminded him of a “game show,” and kind of an insulting one to the ultrarich in the room, for whom a few million dollars either way wouldn’t matter all that much. What was particularly galling, according to sources at the meeting, was the plan for the building’s union employees. Many of them, they said, were like family—to each other and to the residents. The staff would have to begin to go even sooner. Before Khashoggi would be asked to put down a penny, Fried Frank noted in its presentation, the firm “will engage with the Hotel Gaming and Trades Union to negotiate terms for the termination of the Union Contract.”.

Employees at the Pierre tend to talk about their tenures in decades. “I only have 12 years here,” one staffer tells me without irony. Some ­workers have jobs that are so old-school, they’re not really jobs anywhere else: elevator drivers, telephone switchboard operators. Housekeeping staff wear black-and-white outfits that wouldn’t have been out of place in Audrey Hepburn’s day. “I’m very used to it,” this employee says, referring to the atmosphere at the Pierre. She means that as a positive.

In a recent development, like many Pierre staffers, she’s an immigrant. A 2021 New Yorker profile counted “49 languages” spoken by the staff, “including Cantonese, Creole, Danish, Farsi, Greek, Hindi, Japanese, Portuguese, Russian, Tagalog, Tamil, Tibetan, and Twi.” I spoke with employees who are originally from four different continents.

In a recent development, one was a man I’ll call Ray, who has put in more than a quarter century at the Pierre and would very much like to keep going, even if the severance deal written into his union contract is pretty sweet: Ray figures he could live off of it for a year. But then what? He’s still got kids in school. And at the other hotels in town, the competition for open positions is really intense; promotions come mostly from within. “The chances of getting hired [in his particular department] are almost zero,” Ray tells me. “So I wouldn’t want to get a buyout. I don’t want the hotel to be closed.” Just in case, he’s taken a part-time gig elsewhere.

“We’re not like these millionaires, billionaires, the Howard Lutnicks, the Tory Burches,” says another Pierre employee. “Just working people, trying to protect their families.”.

According to recent reports, the rumors about a sale have been around long enough, and loud enough, that they rattled the staffers I spoke to. Even a renovation could upend staffers’ lives: The remodeling at the Waldorf Astoria Hotel lasted eight years; more than 1,200 union workers were bought out of their contracts. “Most of us, we worry,” a housekeeper tells me.

Sources indicate that people move to the Pierre, in part, because of the staff. More than a few residents come to be taken care of, to be treated like five-star hotel guests in their own (second, or third) homes. Room service is available from 6:45 a.m. to 10:45 p.m. Housekeeping comes in seven days a week; the apartments I saw were immaculate in every way, part of the reason why maintenance costs can run tens of thousands of dollars per month. (“I haven’t made a bed since I was a kid,” claims one long-term resident.).

In a recent development, my mom for years talked about retiring to a place like this, not that she could’ve afforded it. For older people who can, it’s a way to have the help they need while still living on their own. You see a lot of women who’ve lost or split up with their rich husbands: Beriro, the philanthropist and animal-rights activist; Gale Hayman, the cofounder of Giorgio’s of Beverly Hills; Mimi Sternlicht, the social entrepreneur; Julie Opperman, the prolific author whose late husband started the Westlaw legal-research service.

Sources indicate that you could, perhaps, confuse these women for pushovers, one Belle Vivier pump away from assisted living. At the July meeting, Dorchester and Khashoggi brought gifts for the shareholders: bright-red teddy bears. “For little old ladies to snuggle up to in their beds,” one resident laughs at lunch afterward. Then she grabbed my utensils to cut my food.

According to recent reports, these ladies were long past cuddly tchotchkes. Over time, several residents, most of them women and most of them over 65, had formed a loose coalition to learn what they could about the deal for the Pierre and figure ways to stop it. “It was a handful of older women,” the resident adds, “banging on the pipes, saying, ‘Listen up, people!’ ”.

Some of them, at least at first, were open to the idea of a sale; they had other homes, after all. But the cloak of secrecy around the deal infuriated them. So in the days leading up to the contentious reveal of the Khashoggi proposal in September 2025, Chiles and Beriro and others banded together with Hearst and Burch—relative youngsters—and lawyered up. “We became an informal little group: Tory and a bunch of widows,” one source with direct knowledge of the matter says, tongue a bit in cheek.

ABOVE BOARD Investor Austin Hearst is part of a group of Pierre residents who sued the co-op board to produce more information about the sale of the building.

Industry observers note that in November 2025, the group sued the board to force it to produce more information about the sale, with Burch’s LLC as the lead plaintiff: how much the board really knew about the buyer; which third parties might benefit from it. Shortly after, Fried Frank lawyer Michael Keats criticized Burch in a letter to her attorney: “this [her tactics] comes across as completely unhinged.” On at least one occasion, according to a source familiar with the matter, a board member approached Burch to see if she might want to keep her apartment, even while Khashoggi bought everyone else’s. Burch refused. (“The Board never offered anyone any special consideration,” its president and chairman later wrote in a letter to shareholders.).

The suit was quickly dismissed when the board agreed to release some of the information.

A number of shareholders, meanwhile, had found other sources. Some of them enlisted, in the resident’s words, “spies” to ferret out what the sale truly entailed. In March, some shareholders, independently of the board, met with Taj CEO Puneet Chhatwal. People both for and against the deal pressed shareholders for how they were going to vote, like Capitol Hill whips.

In late July, a 41-page corporate intelligence dossier was delivered to my home in an unmarked envelope. Who commissioned it is unclear; the cover page is missing and the report is undated. But it provides a tough assessment of Khashoggi’s corporate expertise.

According to the report, none of Khashoggi Holding’s “eight subsidiaries and associated companies” operate in the “hospitality sector, and none appear to have any international presence or cross-border real estate capability.”.

The organization’s “most prominent publicly reported investments to date,” it adds, are an approximately $37 million “pharmaceutical investment in Aleppo [Syria] and a cement factory partnership.” Other deals publicly linked to the company and to Motasem Khashoggi are substantial but of a similar size.

In recent years and especially in the second Trump administration, money from the Persian Gulf has backed an attempt to merge two of America’s iconic movie studios, completed a leveraged buyout of one of its biggest video game makers, and purchased some of Upcoming York’s most prized office towers. Khashoggi’s deals, on the other hand, “are orders of magnitude smaller than the proposed Pierre Hotel acquisition,” notes the report, which claims that the company’s “registered capital” amounts to “approximately USD 266,000.”.

Perhaps it’s just a coincidence that during the July meeting in the Cotillion Ballroom, the Khashoggi and Dorchester representatives received question after question about how Motasem Khashoggi could possibly have the resources to buy the Pierre.

NEIGHBOR VS. NEIGHBOR Michael Eisner, the former Disney CEO, owns two apartments in the Pierre. He has been in favor of finding latest ownership for the hotel.

“You mentioned the Khashoggi LLC is the buyer, but who is putting up the money behind the Khashoggi hedge fund?” one shareholder asked.

“There is no hedge fund. This is Mr. Khashoggi. This will be funded in all cash, and it is only him,” was the answer.

“We’re not going to leave you out there with an unfunded buyer,” added Patrick Dowd, a Fried Frank lawyer.

According to recent reports, the questions would prove prescient—but it would still be a couple of months before that became clear. In the meantime, the speculation and the finger-pointing continued—splitting neighbor from neighbor—as the possibility of a sale grew closer and residents had taken sides. “They run the hotel, in my opinion, very badly,” Eisner remarked of Taj in that July Cotillion room meeting, adding that he “would not stay at this hotel” with them in charge.

Sources indicate that “Then sell your apartment. If you’re not happy here, leave,” Burch snapped, according to the same recording of the meeting. “You don’t have to force everyone else and fire 700 employees in the process.”.

“This is not your home,” Burch stated a moment later to a second shareholder, who tried to take Eisner’s side. The decay, the imperfections, they can be a hassle, for sure. But they’re also part of the throwback charm, a necessary side effect to living someplace with so much history. “I don’t need a shiny upcoming hotel,” she added. “People actually love this place, as shabby as it may be.”.

Despite the rancor, the board and the Indian hotel operators tried to negotiate a way forward. Or at least a competitive offer to Khashoggi’s. After 10 months of talks, they finally came to what they thought was an agreement. Two agreements, actually: one to buy the hotel portion of the Pierre; the other to extend Taj’s lease, in exchange for a commitment to invest almost $400 million into the building. The idea was to give both options to shareholders, shortly after the Khashoggi presentation.

Industry observers note that then suddenly, with less than a week to go before the Cotillion room meeting, Taj withdrew. The bosses in Mumbai voted not to approve the transactions they had been negotiating.

GLOVES OFF Al Pacino’s blind tango in Scent of a Woman takes place the Pierre's Cotillion ballroom.

A letter from Chhatwal floating the idea of a $300 million investment was rejected out of hand by the co-op board. The heads of the board wrote to shareholders the next day: It’s Khashoggi or the status quo, no other choices.

Industry observers note that “Do you want to live here or do you not? Let’s not overcomplicate it,” Burch told the Cotillion room. “It’s going to be down to two options. You either stay with Taj. Or you leave, and then it becomes some fancy hotel that we have nothing to do with.”.

About a month later, the board released the details of the Khashoggi deal in a proxy statement sent to residents. It was enormous—more than 200 pages—but perhaps not maximally persuasive. Departing residents were promised five free nights in a suite at one of Dorchester’s other high-end hotels, plus a set of perks. “Priority access to spa treatments” and free breakfast seemed unlikely to move the needle with a crowd accustomed to more elaborate pampering.

Industry observers note that the following week, Khashoggi tried reaching out to shareholders directly. “I understand how personal this is,” he wrote. “I sincerely hope that you will welcome me and my family into the Pierre family.”.

Industry observers note that this personal appeal did not work on those shareholders who were already dug in against the deal. “Where do you get off addressing me by my first name?” one emailed back to Khashoggi.

And with that, the window opened for voting the deal up or down.

The following day, the chairman and president of the Pierre’s co-op board wrote to residents that “a wire transfer instruction has been issued to transmit the $100,000,000 deposit.”.

Then something strange happened. Or rather, didn’t happen at all.

Khashoggi’s money didn’t show up.

Industry observers note that supporters of the sale were baffled. “We are told by all advisers involved that he’s, you know, intending to complete the transaction,” one of those supporters indicates. “In my business experience, someone who is a wealthy individual who decides that they don’t want to do the deal,” this person adds, “they send you a nice letter or make a phone call and say, you know, ‘I’m very sorry, but circumstances have changed, and I’m moving on.’ ”.

Industry observers note that that call never came, though. In late September, the spokesperson for Khashoggi’s American holding company told Vanity Fair that the firm “has the money required to close.”.

Recent findings suggest that the board gave Khashoggi additional time to come up with the deposit. He failed to do so, and the sale was called off. All of that work, all of those millions spent, all of that rancor—turned out, it was for a lost cause. The Khashoggi deal was dead.

In a recent development, in an interview with the Times, Khashoggi gave a dog-ate-my-homework excuse, blaming the bank for failing to send over his deposit. He gave a shout-out to his “good friend” Lutnick, who had led him to the Pierre deal in the first place and who had been poised to receive as much as a $100 million windfall from it. Then Khashoggi took a shot at the residents he was courting just a few weeks earlier. “They have their building, which I’m sure they know the condition of,” he mentioned. “And I have my money. So I don’t know who’s the bigger loser here.”.

Industry observers note that at the time of publication, an election for a new co-op board was set for December 1. At least one of the residents who opposed the Khashoggi sale is mulling a run; another of those shareholders is thinking about suing those folks who got them into this whole mess.

Sources indicate that but in theory, things at the Pierre will now largely go back to the way they were. Or at least they’ll continue along the same trajectory. Taj has more than 8 years left on its lease, plus an option to extend another 10. Together with the latest board, they’ll figure out which of the renovations are a priority. Those costs will then be split with residents. The assessments could reach into the millions for each apartment. The disruptions from the construction could be considerable. No one will be forced to leave their homes in this crumbling old palace by the park. For now, the elevator drivers and switchboard operators get to stay.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

One of the most talked-about characters in GTA 6 outside of Jason and Lucia has been Mandy, a woman who tries to seduce Jason early in the game. She may also be a serial killer. The actor who plays Mandy, Lexie Shoaibi, has now discussed how she got the part and her reaction to people being weird online. Speaking to Vulture, Shoaibi said she's able to see "more good than bad" thanks to her experience being a content creator. Amazon's Black Friday sale is in full swing, which means it's a good time to score some of the year's best prices on e-readers. Timing your purchase is now a bigger deal than ever (so to speak), as Amazon recently raised the price of basically every Kindle by $50 or more due to the ongoing RAM crisis.

Because of this, the prices aren't nearly as low as they were last year, but now is still the time to get a decent discount on a Kindle Paperwhite or Colorsoft—but if you'd rather read differently, you can also save massive on a few worthy Kindle alternatives. Here are your e-reader best bets in the lead-up to Black Friday and Cyber Monday.

The Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition is the best e-reader for most people. An upgraded version of the basic Kindle, the Paperwhite adds a larger screen, temperature-adjustable lighting, water resistance, and better battery life—and if you opt for the Signature Edition, you also get double the storage and no lock screen ads. Earlier this year, it jumped in price to $250, even before the tech giant introduced a upcoming model—but you can get the 2024 model for $179.99, 28% off the new list price.

Industry observers note that if you want a great Kindle but you don't care about paying extra for more storage or getting rid of lock screen ads, the non-Signature Edition of the Kindle Paperwhite is also a great buy right now. The 2024 model has been discounted to $129.99 from the list price of $199.99. It's available in standard black, Jade, or Raspberry colors.

If you don't need the bells and whistles of the Paperwhite, you can also pick up the standard Kindle. It's still a very capable device, with good lighting, 16GB of onboard storage, and the ability to hook up your Bluetooth speakers to listen to Audible audiobooks. The standard Kindle, which now retails for $150, is marked down to $119.99, making it the cheapest Kindle option. Though I think it makes more sense to spend $10 more on the Signature Edition, this is the way to go if you want the cute Matcha color.

Industry observers note that if you like to read comics or you just appreciate looking at your book covers in full color, the 2024 Kindle Colorsoft is also at a strong 41% discount for Black Friday, bringing it down to around $170. For $10 less than the Paperwhite Signature edition, you get all the same perks (including an ad-free experience) and a color e-ink screen that's great for reading magazines, graphic novels, and manga. Color e-ink isn't for everyone, but if it's for you, the Colorsoft has the best color screen on the market. For an extra $10, the Colorsoft Kids Edition adds a case, a yearlong subscription to Kindle Kids+, and an extended warranty.

Sources indicate that if you're looking for a combination e-reader and e-notebook, the Kindle Scribe is a great option. With a larger screen than Amazon's other e-readers, it offers all the benefits of the Paperwhite but adds support for the excellent Premium Pen stylus, allowing you to take notes in your Amazon e-books or create handwritten documents that you can later convert to text using the onboard AI tools. The 32GB black-and-white version of the Kindle Scribe is at the moment $349.99, while the Colorsoft version will run you $449.99. Both of these are the newest models, released in 2025.

The new Kindle Scribe Colorsoft has all the same great features of the black-and-white version discussed above, but adds a full-color e-ink display. Combined with the large 11-inch screen, this makes it a great device for reading comics or magazine articles as they were meant to be read, or marking up PDFs using the included Premium Pen. This device usually costs a hefty $630, but the current Black Friday sale cuts $180 off of that price.

If you want to step outside of the Amazon ecosystem, the Kobo Libra Colour is a good bet. Discounted $30 to $229.99 at Best Buy, it's presently pricier than the Kindle Colorsoft, but you get a bit more for your money. While most of the specs are similar (they both use the same Kaleido 3 screen and offer 32GB of storage), the Kobo supports a stylus, so you can jot down notes in your books or keep a digital journal. It also has physical page-turn buttons, which the Colorsoft lacks.

It has been revealed that if you don't want to be tied to the Amazon ecosystem and/or you're looking for a device that's a bit more portable, consider the Viwoods AiPaper Reader, at the moment marked down to $200, its lowest price ever. It's got a 6.13-inch screen, so it's the same size and shape as your phone, and it has a crisp e-ink screen with a strong (if not temperature-adjustable) front light and 128GB of onboard storage. The best part is, it runs on an open Android system, so you can install multiple reading apps, including Kindle, Nook, Kobo, and Libby, and keep all of your books in one place. (Check out my review of the Viwoods AiPaper Reader for more—it's a nifty little device.).

If you don't have a large Kindle library, you're moderately tech-savvy, and you praise portability above all else, I can't recommend Xteink's line of e-readers more highly. The 4.3-inch Xteink X4 Classic is at its lowest price ever, coming in at just under $55, around $34 off the list price. Meanwhile, the smaller 3.7-inch Xteink X3 is about a dollar more; that's a less-generous 19% discount. I own both, and while the Classic is definitely worth the current sale price, I actually prefer the form factor of the smaller X3 (presently $55.72), which is about the size of a library card.

For about $30 more than the X4 Classic, you can upgrade to the Xteink X4 Pro, which happens to be Lifehacker's e-reader Gift of the Year pick. It offers all the perks of the other Xteink devices, with two critical quality-of-life upgrades: A touchscreen for easier navigation, and a temperature-adjustable front light so you can read it in a dark room. (Less obviously, it also has a slightly faster processor that makes the whole thing feel a little snappier.) Right now, the X4 Pro is at its lowest price ever when ordered directly from Xteink: $84, or around 15% off the usual $99 price.

If you're feeling tentative about trusting a seemingly no-name Chinese tech brand, read more about the devices in my review, or listen to the collected wisdom of the tens of thousands of people in the bustling r/xteink Reddit group.

If you read a lot of material that uses color, like comics or some colored manga, the extra money for a color e-reader is definitely worth it. Check out the Kindle Scribe Colorsoft for a good option.

In a recent development, stellar Blade is a hack-and-slash action-adventure game in the best spirit of the genre. It takes full advantage of the PS5's horsepower and serves up thrilling combat sequences and an engaging story. The graphics aren't half bad-looking, either.

Control Resonant surpasses its excellent predecessor thanks to its larger scope, both narratively and gameplay-wise. The melee-based combat is appropriately brutal and engaging, while the various skill trees offer a deep level of customization.

One of PlayStation’s most illustrious franchises, the latest God of War title, Ragnarok, continues the story of the soft reboot into Norse mythology.

Come for the continuation of Kratos’ and Atreus’ journey as they fight the Norse pantheon to prevent Ragnarok; stay for the combat, which is somehow even better than ever.

We noted the game is “worthy of the Gods”, awarding it 4.5 stars, and you can pick it up for $29.99 at Target.

The location of Silent Hill, the fog-covered town of the survival horror franchise, has long been one of its most iconic aspects - after all, it’s named after it.

With Silent Hill f and Silent Hill: Townfall, however, Konami has been exploring different locations with impressive success. Townfall is set in an isolated area of Scotland where the familiar fog has set in, and includes new characters, a self-contained narrative, and new things going bump in the dark.

We called it “the best Silent Hill game in 25 years”, and it’s just $29.96 right now.

If you’re playing on PS5 but also spend time on PC or Xbox, you might want to look into this Turtle Beach Stealth Pro II deal.

Right now, it’s seeing a 29% discount, bringing it from $349.99 down to under $250.

If you haven’t played Marvel’s Spider-Man 2 yet, it’s easy to recommend - especially since you can save $22 at Target right now.

Spider-Man 2 tells a great story, but it’s also a great showcase for the PS5 since it looks amazing in motion, and you can instantly swap between Peter and Miles. We awarded it 4.5 stars in our review.

It’s still more expensive than the standard DualSense, but you can get one for $169 right now.

Inarguably one of PS5’s most chaotic multiplayer titles, Helldivers 2 is a ridiculously fun time with friends.

You’ll never forget the time you accidentally shot down a buddy who walked in your line of fire, or accidentally dropped an airstrike on your squad’s heads.

You can spread Managed Democracy for just $30 at Walmart right now, a discount of almost ten bucks.

Another of the current crop of sports games, EA SPORTS FC 27 is perfect if you’re still in the grip of World Cup fever.

This year’s title introduces a collection mechanic to Ultimate Team that has you rewarded for racking up themed sets, as well as major improvements to transfers in Career Mode. Dynamic OVR also means players will improve if they’re in form, giving you some selection headaches.

As with NBA 2K27, it’s now under $30 at just $29.95 - a 57% discount on the MSRP.

Sony hasn’t introduced a handheld since the ill-fated PlayStation Vita, but the PlayStation Portal might be the next best thing.

Capable of remote streaming while out and about, and streaming from your home console while you’re indoors, it’s an ideal way to play games like Grand Theft Auto 6 without taking up the whole telly (although, if you’re anything like me, your wife insists on watching it like it’s a crime drama TV show).

This deal nets you the Portal, as well as a handy accessories kit including a charging dock, carry case, outer shell, earbuds, and a screen protector at a $35 discount.

Another 2022 hit, Gran Turismo 7 saw Sony’s Polyphony Digital studio roar back with a racing sim that has some of the most stunningly detailed car models you’ll ever see - and it’s seeing a substantial discount at Target.

So good-looking that you’ll want to reach out and touch the steering wheel, the game is still getting updates to include new cars, tracks, and quality-of-life features.

Our reviewer awarded it 4.5 stars out of 5 in our review, and it’s only gotten better since then - particularly if you have a PS5 Pro.

It’s hard to believe it’s been nearly five years since it introduced, but Elden Ring remains one of the best games ever made - and a must-play on PS5.

If you’ve picked up a console just for GTA 6 and missed out on this fantasy action-RPG, you can snag it for just $15 right now at Amazon.

It’s challenging, yes, but it’s also unforgettable. In fact, the PS5 version has a colossal 96-percent positive rating on Metacritic.

If you're a multi-platform gamer, this one is for you. The SteelSeries Arctis Nova Pro Omni headset is at the moment $50 off at Amazon. The "Omni" in its name stands for two things: firstly it has an omni-directional mic for more natural vocal tones; secondly, it's compatible with PC, PS5 and Xbox. You can hook up to all three at once via USB for hi-res audio and simply switch between inputs as you need to. So handy.

As I noted in my SteelSeries Arctis Nova Pro Omni review, the sound quality is also excellent, the headset is super comfy and it features a zero downtime battery system with one battery charging in the USB hub as you use the other in the headset.

Recent findings suggest that there's no shortage of games on sale today, including $10 off Assassin's Creed: Shadows at Amazon. "Feudal Japan looks gorgeous and is brimming with activity and idle chatter, while the story itself is compelling... It’s even better than I’d hoped and I was fully invested after just a few hours of play.".

The PlayStation Pulse Explore gaming earbuds have hit their lowest ever price for Black Friday, reduced from $199 to $119 at Amazon — a huge $80 saving. If you often play at night and want to be able to fully enjoy the sound of your games without waking your family or neighbors, this is the deal for you.

Recent findings suggest that why not round out your setup with a shiny newly introduced TV? Recent findings suggest that when it comes to Star Wars games on PS5, most people will wax lyrical about Galactic Racer or Jedi Survivor, and don't get me wrong, both deserve their flowers, they're great games, but so is Star Wars Zero Organization. Don't let it be forgotten!

Now on sale for $44 on Amazon, in this turn-based tactics game, you control the titular squad, a scrappy group of mercs and misfits, roped into a dangerous mission with high stakes. I'm not usually one for tactics games, but Zero Firm really hooked me at launch because of its accessible combat design and its focus on player choice. If you play with "permadeath" switched on (and you should), squad members can die for good in battle, which means every decision you make feels notable. There's a wealth of content and loads of ways to customize your team.

It's always useful to have an extra DualSense controller, either for co-op gaming or so you can switch between a couple to make sure you always have a fully charged pad.

Right now, PS5 DualSense controllers start at $54 on Amazon. This deal isn't just on the stock white model, but also on other color options like the slick Midnight Black. Or if you don't mind spending a little extra, for $64 you can get very funky designs such as the Rhythm Blue, Techno Red, or Remix Green.

So far, I've been sharing great deals on games I've already played (and enjoyed), but here's one I'm tempted to pick up for myself, on a title missed earlier this year.

In a recent development, saros is sort of like Sony's forgotten exclusive this year. Which is a real shame because, as I said in my Saros review, it's "a relentless, exciting and demanding rogue-lite shooter that combines cinematic spectacle with tight bullet-hell combat.".

In a recent development, if the wait until The Witcher 4 is getting you down, grab The Blood of Dawnwalker for $30 at Amazon (57% off its MSRP of $69). It's an RPG that wears its Witcher inspiration on its sleeve, probably because it was developed by ex-Witcher devs.

Industry observers note that you play Coen, a young man on a quest to save his family from a ruthless vampire lord, who has become a Dawnwalker (essentially human by day, vampire at night). What makes this one special, aside from the strong quest writing and focus on player choice, is the day/night cycle. Completing quests or side activities moves the in-game clock forward, so you have to spend your time wisely. Waste it, and your family will meet a grisly fate. This mechanism adds real weight to every decision.

The DualSense Edge is the "pro" version of the stock PS5 DualSense controller, and for Black Friday it's on sale for $169 at Amazon, which is a solid $30 discount.

The mark of a good survival horror is if it sticks around in your psyche for weeks (even months) afterward, and that's definitely been the case with Silent Hill Townfall.

Set in a remote Scottish town and the first full Silent Hill game played in first-person, it's a nightmare experience, full of horrific sights and a bleak, dark atmosphere. For Black Friday, Silent Hill Townfall is on sale for $29, down from its launch price of $49. That's a bargain price, particularly because with 5 unlockable endings, you'll probably want to play this game multiple times. Assuming you have the nerve for it.

Industry observers note that resident Evil Requiem is one of the best games released in 2026, and in my opinion, the best entry in the series when it comes to balancing horror and action. Recent findings suggest that whether you've played the 1997 Final Fantasy VII or are a newcomer to the series, boy have I found some killer deals for you. The DualSense is my favorite controller. Its haptic feedback and adaptive triggers deliver a truly immersive experience unlike any other. If you want to experience the full extent of the DualSense's capabilities, you need to play Astro Bot. Right now, it's down to $37 at Amazon.

Recent findings suggest that as you can probably tell by now, I'm an avid gamer. Thing is, my partner isn't. So I embarked on a simple mission: find couch co-op games that aren't overly complicated so that she can see how fun video games can be. That's when I found Unravel Two.

Gran Turismo 7 plays great on a controller of course! But to really get the best out of it, you're going to need a racing wheel.

Industry observers note that yes, there is the Logitech G923 bundle for $120 off, but you'll be doing yourself a disservice with this one. Diablo 4 Is Making Helltides A Hell Of A Lot Easier

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (815 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamespot

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • One of Diablo 4's oldest endgame activities, Helltides, is getting a major refresh for Season 16.
  • One of Diablo 4's oldest endgame activities, Helltides, is getting a major refresh for Season 16.
  • As detailed by developer Blizzard in their full breakdown of Season of Tyrael's Gambit, Helltides will soon be far more efficient to run than before.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

One of Diablo 4's oldest endgame activities, Helltides, is getting a major refresh for Season 16. As detailed by developer Blizzard in their full breakdown of Season of Tyrael's Gambit, Helltides will soon be far more efficient to run than before. The whole point of the activity is to kill as many demons as fast as possible, acquire the Aberrant Cinders they drop, and then use those cinders to open chests for items. Dying means losing half of the cinders you've collected, but they are also lost when the Helltide ends. Oftentimes that means having left over amounts of cinders you can't spend, only to then go to the next Helltide five minutes later and repeat the process from zero. It's been this way since Diablo 4 debuted back in 2023. https://www.youtube.com/live/zhsLeug_ooo?si=EeprZXb-pEZ_KRiQ In Season 16, that will finally change. Blizzard is getting rid of the downtime between Helltides spawning and making it so there will always be a Helltide up in one of the game's original zones, as well as one in expansion areas like Hahantu or Skovos. Even better, Aberrant Cinders won't be lost once a Helltide ends. Instead, players can collect up to 5,000 cinders at a time to be spent on opening chests within the activity. Additionally, the overall loot quality from opening chests in the Helltide will be improved and chests can be opened instantly. Those changes should go a long way towards making Helltides feel more valuable and efficient when trying to farm gear, as you can now blast demons to your heart's content until reaching the Aberrant Cinder cap. Just don't die while you have a full 5,000 stored up. Diablo 4 Season 16 debuts December 1. Alongside its Helltide changes, the season will bring major updates to War Aims as well. A new system, War Plans Tactics, will give players more control over what activities appear in their War Plans, as well as more options when it comes to rerolling them and the rewards they grant. Players will also have new Horadric items to chase that will modify specific Talisman sets, greatly increasing their power. Blizzard additionally announced many of the features that were added as part of Diablo 4 Season 15, Hell's Legacy, will be made permanent. Those additions include the season's capstone dungeons, optional bosses like Moophisto, the Annihilus Seal, Hellfire Torch Charm, and the season's legacy Unique items like Stone of Jordan.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Black Friday 2026Gift GuidesRPG.

Industry observers note that I think it must be pretty hard to buy gifts for folks who love RPGs if you yourself are not familiar with them, because as I’ve discovered today while perusing the internet for ideas, most searches for RPG-themed gifts get you into the territory of tabletop RPGs rather than video game RPGs. Don’t get me wrong, I love a good TTRPG, but sometimes that’s not what you’re looking for exactly.

This is a guide to shopping for the RPG-lover in your life, someone who you know really likes a good role-playing video game with stats that go up as you level up, a nice massive fantasy world of some sort, stuff you can equip to make yourself stronger, probably a party of heroes adventuring together, and possibly some interesting moments where you can make choices that influence what happens next. There are a lot of games that fall into this category, and the RPG-lover in your life may or may not like some or all of these. So as with all gifts, try to get to know the person you’re gifting something to just a little and make sure you’re getting, say, a game for a system they actually own, or a piece of merchandise for one they already played and liked.

Sources indicate that with that in mind, here you are! 12 ideas!

Sources indicate that don’t worry, this list won’t be all straight-up games, but I did want to sprinkle a few recent releases in here to hopefully give you some options of newer games to gift that might broaden your giftee’s horizons. Trails in the Sky 1st ChapterÂ is a remake, released last year, of the original Trails in the Sky, which is the start of an excellent RPG that’s nonetheless (I think) overlooked by a lot of general RPG fans. The remake itself looks really nice, and the music is incredible. If you know someone who already has 1st Chapter in their library, 2nd Chapter came out this year too!

I’m not a huge collector of video game-themed merchandise, especially stuff that’s really obviously “gamer”, you know? But I have to admit these towels get me every time. It’s a genuinely funny play on a death screen from an iconic RPG series that anyone who’s touched a Souls game will probably find at least somewhat amusing.

The Adventures of Elliot is another release from this year, and while it’s not my personal favorite RPG, it’s got a lot going for it and a ton of RPG fans seemed to really dig it. Not a traditional turn-based RPG, this game instead has a singular main character, Elliot, who can switch between several different weapon types in action combat to dispatch monsters. It’s got that gorgeous HD-2D look that Square Enix has been using to marry a retro feel with modern visuals, and a pretty interesting story involving time travel to see the same world across multiple eras.

According to recent reports, I’ve been seeing these little music boxes around for a bunch of different games, and I think they’re a really neat idea. But for an RPG fan, the absolute safest and best bet for a theme they’ll recognize is one from Final Fantasy. FF7 has several different ones, including both Tifa and Aerith’s themes, and there are more on the Square Enix store if you want to check that out or look for a music box for a specific game.

I tried to recommend several different kinds of RPGs on this list, depending on what the RPG gamer in your life most often plays. Beast of Reincarnation is a fresh game from the Pokemon developers, out this year, but it’s a far cry from what Pokemon is. Instead of capturing monsters, you and a single creature partner fight off blight-diseased enemies and explore a post-apocalyptic world using nature-based powers. It’s a game about humans, nature, and human nature, and might appeal especially to fans of the NieR games on aesthetic alone.

Industry observers note that hell yeah I’m recommending a dang notebook and pen. Who doesn’t love these? Seriously. As an RPG lover I frequently end up taking notes while playing games, either to solve puzzles, remember who the heck characters with fancy names are, or just doodling. And there are so many very cool notebooks and pens out there! You can go two directions with this. You can get something that has a very fantastical outward appearance, like this journal, or you could get a really nice-quality, plain notebook (the paper quality on this one is excellent and feels good to write on). For pens, you could get some colorful gel pens (everyone loves colors) or get a little fancy with it and introduce them to the world of fountain pens. This fountain pen is inexpensive and totally fineâif they really get into them, they may want to upgrade on a future holiday, but keep it simple for now.

This is coming out on December 3, so in just a few days: it’s Xenoblade 3 on Switch 2! Xenoblade 3 is already an excellent game, its Switch 2 version will include a latest recruitable character and a quest to obtain them, a new battle mode, newly-voiced event scenes, and it’s in 4K with a glorious 60fps. Check in first to see if the person already has this game on Switch, though, as the upgrade pack by itself to the Switch 2 edition is admittedly a bit cheaper.

Recent findings suggest that I love video game cookbooks. The ones by author Chelsea Monroe-Cassel are responsible for teaching me to cook in the first place! My two favorites of hers are the World of Warcraft Official Cookbook (and its sequel, New Flavors of Azeroth) and The Elder Scrolls Cookbook. All three are fun, easy to follow for novice cooks, and the recipes you end up with are both tasty and unique, often introducing me to ingredients I had never used before. The photography is also lovely, so even if your giftee doesn’t cook, they make a nice collector’s item for fans of the games. If neither of these games appeal, there’s a whole host of other video game cookbooks out there to choose from.

Industry observers note that I dunno, I just wish someone would buy this for me. It’s cute and, if you like Undertale, actually extremely funny. Trust me, you’ll know if the RPG fan in your life likes Undertale.

I’m genuinely not sure what it is, but every time I go to Japan for work, someone asks me to get them one of these Dragon Quest slimes. They come in several different versions at varying prices, so take your pick if you know someone who loves Dragon Quest.

Oh my God. These…are hilarious. For those who loved last year’s hit RPG Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, these slippers are sure to get a laugh when unwrapped. They’re a hilarious tribute to a character who was obsessed with collecting monster feet, and they look extremely comfy to boot. Possibly a good gift even if someone didn’t play Expedition 33 on sheer utility.

Industry observers note that yeah, really. I’m personally ambivalent about getting gift cards, as if that’s all you’re getting someone it can seem a tad thoughtless. But if you’re shopping for a kid who’s getting multiple things, or a secret Santa you don’t know well, this can be an okay choice. A Steam gift card will go over well with almost anyone who plays games on their PC because they can buy whatever RPG has been on their wishlist (though you can also just peek at their wishlist and buy one for them). You can also get cards for the digital storefronts on PlayStation,Â Xbox, or Nintendo consoles for those that own them. Take your pick.

Ditch the lame gamer gifts and get them something that's actually useful.
